title: Shiksha Copilot: Teacher-AI Collaboration for Curating and Customizing Lesson Plans in Low-Resource Schools
extended_summary:
This paper examines how teachers in low-resource schools collaborate with an AI-assisted lesson planning system, Shiksha Copilot, to create and adapt curriculum-aligned lesson plans. The core question is not only whether generative AI can produce usable instructional materials, but how teachers actually review, customize, and integrate AI-generated plans into their work in multilingual, resource-constrained settings.

Shiksha Copilot combined LLM-based generation, retrieval-augmented generation over textbook content, human curation, bilingual English-Kannada translation, and optional teacher-facing AI tools such as lesson-specific chat and question generation. The system was developed for government schools in Karnataka, India, and deployed to 1,043 teachers teaching grades 5–10 across Kannada- and English-medium public schools. The study used a mixed-methods design with system logs, surveys, and interviews, plus a curation phase involving 23 subject curators.

The findings show that AI-generated lesson plans were generally reliable in English but required heavy linguistic revision in Kannada. Teachers used the tool both for instruction and for bureaucratic record-keeping, and the system reduced planning time and stress while supporting a shift toward more activity-based pedagogy. At the same time, teachers often adapted content mentally or off-platform, and broader change was constrained by structural issues such as administrative demands, staffing shortages, and language/translation quality problems. The paper concludes that effective teacher-AI collaboration depends on human oversight, contextual adaptation, and community-based curation, especially in low-resource and multilingual settings.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed mixed-methods field deployment with surveys, interviews, and log analysis, but it is not a randomized or quasi-experimental causal impact study. The evidence is strong for implementation and user-perceived outcomes, but weaker for attributing changes to the intervention alone.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports clear operational benefits for a priority population of teachers in low-resource schools, especially reduced planning burden and improved access to materials. However, the impact is mostly modest/qualitative, with no direct student achievement effect sizes and substantial constraints on scalability and language quality.

interventions.use_case: teacher-facing LLM-based lesson planning and curriculum-aligned content generation with human-in-the-loop curation, bilingual English-Kannada support, lesson-specific chat, general education chat, and question-generation tools for K-12 teachers
teacher-supported digital lesson-plan distribution and customization platform for classroom instructional planning in low-resource K-12 schools

finding.finding_summary: Shiksha Copilot reduced bureaucratic workload and lesson-planning burden for teachers in low-resource Karnataka schools. Survey and interview evidence indicate measurable reductions in lesson-planning time and teacher stress, with teachers using the tool to generate and customize lesson plans for both instructional delivery and record-keeping; the paper does not report a single pooled effect size for these outcomes.
finding.measure: Teacher-reported lesson-planning time, administrative/record-keeping workload, and teacher stress (Teacher Stress Scale)
finding.study_size: n=406 matched survey responses; n=22 teacher interviews; platform logs from 5,544 teacher-created lesson plans

finding.finding_summary: The system supported broader organizational and institutional workflows by helping teachers satisfy administrative documentation requirements and fit state-mandated lesson-plan formats (e.g., 5E). However, the paper also reports that staffing shortages and administrative demands limited broader pedagogical change, so the institutional impact was meaningful but constrained.
finding.measure: Qualitative interview themes about documentation compliance, workflow integration, and organizational change
finding.study_size: n=43 interviews; n=23 curators; n=1,043 teachers in deployment

finding.finding_summary: The tool improved access to curriculum-aligned lesson plans and shifted some teachers toward activity-based pedagogy, but the paper does not provide student learning outcome measures. Curators reported high reliability in English lesson plans (96.13% of content blocks suitable for classroom use, 4.1% edited), while Kannada translations required extensive revision (94.4% of blocks edited), indicating stronger academic utility in English than in Kannada.
finding.measure: Curator ratings of lesson-plan quality, edit rates by content block, and teacher reports of pedagogical use
finding.study_size: 991 curated lesson plans (965 English, 26 Kannada); 5,544 teacher-created lesson plans
